findings.issue: 'lancheira' in pt-BR denotes the container (a child's lunchbox/bag), not the boxed meal itself. It is effectively the gloss of 弁当箱, not 弁当, and teaches the learner the wrong referent. 'marmita' and 'bentô' already cover the sense correctly.

Gloss 'throughout/all through' belongs to the homograph 中 read じゅう (JMdict 1585730, e.g. 一日中・世界中), not to 中/ちゅう, whose JMdict senses are 'during; while; under (construction)'. Conflates the two readings; the pt mirror 'ao longo de/por todo' must be dropped/reassigned too.
findings.suggested: (delete this gloss — 'throughout' is 中 read じゅう, a different lexeme; keep only the 'during/in the middle of' gloss)
findings.fix: (delete this gloss — 'throughout' is 中 read じゅう, a different lexeme; keep only the 'during/in the middle of' gloss)

findings.issue: First pt gloss 'sem graça (comida)' means 'bland/flavorless', weaker than まずい 'bad-tasting'; it does not render the en glosses 'bad-tasting, unappetizing'. The faithful glosses ('ruim de sabor', 'intragável') should lead.

Sense belongs to the homophone 合う (JMdict 1284430), not 会う (1198180), whose only JMdict senses are 'to meet/encounter/see' and 'to have an accident/bad experience' (esp. 遭う). Remove the whole sense, incl. pt 'combinar, cair bem, ajustar-se'.
findings.current: to fit, to suit, to match
findings.suggested: (remove sense — 'to fit/suit/match' is 合う, a different verb)
findings.fix: (remove sense — 'to fit/suit/match' is 合う, a different verb)

findings.issue: Standalone 伯(はく) has no 'uncle' sense; JMdict 1474240 senses are count/earl, ritsuryō chief official (hist), Brazil (abbr). 'Uncle' is the word 伯父(おじ) / the kanji's role in compounds. Remove the sense, incl. pt 'tio'.
findings.suggested: (remove sense — 'uncle' is 伯父, not a sense of standalone 伯)
findings.fix: (remove sense — 'uncle' is 伯父, not a sense of standalone 伯)

findings.issue: 'Rank/degree/grade' is the separate noun lexeme 位(くらい) (JMdict 1154330), not this suf/prt entry (1154340: approximately; to the extent that; as...as). Gloss also contradicts the sense's suf/prt pos. Remove the sense, incl. pt 'posição, grau'.
findings.suggested: (remove sense — noun 'rank/grade' is a separate 位 entry, not this particle/suffix)
findings.fix: (remove sense — noun 'rank/grade' is a separate 位 entry, not this particle/suffix)

findings.issue: 何(なん) has no exclamatory 'how' sense — that is 何と/なんて (separate entries). JMdict 2846738 sense 2 is the must-know prefix 'how many' before a counter (何時, 何人, 何歳), which is missing. Replace en and pt (pt → 'quantos, quantas (antes de contador)').
findings.suggested: how many (before a counter, e.g. 何時, 何人)
findings.fix: how many (before a counter, e.g. 何時, 何人)

findings.issue: Two EN glosses are joined into a single array element with a comma, unlike every other entry in the batch which stores one gloss per element. Content itself is correct (kasa = umbrella; parasol).
notes: en array holds one comma-joined element 'umbrella, parasol' while its own pt array splits into 2 items and every other batch entry is one gloss per element; real schema defect, split fix correct.

findings.issue: Gloss 'aquilo' belongs to あれ (distal demonstrative), not それ. The EN gloss itself specifies '(near the listener)', which maps to isso/esse in pt-BR; aquilo/aquele maps to あれ. Including 'aquilo' breaks the ko-so-a-do correspondence the course must teach and conflates two contrasting words.

'a frente' (article + noun, 'the front') is a crase/spelling error for the adverbial meaning 'in front' that it is meant to render (EN 'in front'); as written it is redundant with 'frente'. Should be 'à frente' or 'na frente'.
'ano após o próximo' is a stilted calque of 'the year after next'; not natural Brazilian phrasing. Meaning is correct but a reviewer would reword it (the first gloss 'daqui a dois anos' is fine).

The 'middle-aged man' sense belongs to the homophone lexeme 小父 (おじさん), not to 叔父. JMdict 1607070 (叔父/伯父) means only 'uncle'. Attaching this sense to hw 叔父 teaches false kanji usage; the pt glosses 'senhor, tio (homem de meia-idade)' inherit the same error.
findings.suggested: (remove this sense; 'middle-aged man' is 小父さん, a separate lexeme)
findings.fix: (remove this sense; 'middle-aged man' is 小父さん, a separate lexeme)

findings.issue: 'moção' in Brazilian Portuguese means almost exclusively a formal/parliamentary motion (moção de repúdio); as a gloss for physical motion it is a misleading calque of English 'motion'. Drop it — 'movimento' already covers the sense.

Sense pos is adv, but glosses are adjectival/nominal ('awful, tough, a big deal') — these belong to the adj-na sense of 大変 (serious; hard; tough). As an adverb 大変 only means 'very/terribly', which sense 0 already covers. Mislabeled sense can teach wrong usage.
findings.suggested: terribly; awfully — or retag this sense adj-na to keep 'awful; hard; tough'
findings.fix: terribly; awfully — or retag this sense adj-na to keep 'awful; hard; tough'

findings.issue: 'gostado' is not used as a standalone adjective in Brazilian Portuguese (gostar is only 'gostar de'; passive/adjectival 'gostado' is unnatural). Reads as a translation artifact of 'liked'.
findings.suggested: querido (or drop; 'gostar de' + 'preferido' already cover the sense)
findings.fix: querido (or drop; 'gostar de' + 'preferido' already cover the sense)

findings.issue: Two glosses packed into one array element ('student, pupil') — every other entry stores one gloss per element. Also 'pupil' better matches 生徒/児童; 学生 is a student, esp. university student.

The sense 'to sting, to bite (insect)' belongs to the homophone 刺す (JMdict 1315520), not 差す. 差す (1291330) means to shine (light), to hold up (an umbrella), to insert/pour — never to sting. Teaches a wrong kanji-meaning pairing.
notes: 差す (1291330) has no sting/bite sense; that is 刺す (1315520), e.g. 蚊に刺された. 'To shine' is JMdict sense 1 of 差す and matches the record's vi POS tag. Real kanji-meaning error.

findings.issue: pt glosses 'picar, ferroar' render the sting/bite sense of the homophone 刺す, which is not a meaning of 差す. Must be replaced together with the EN gloss of this sense.
notes: picar/ferroar render 刺す, not 差す; must change with the EN sense. 'brilhar (sol, luz)' is an acceptable pt-BR gloss of 日が差す for a learner dictionary.

findings.issue: Glosses belong to the homophone 彼(かれ) 'he' (JMdict 1483150). This record's kana is あれ: 彼(あれ) is the distal demonstrative 'that / that thing'. As written the entry teaches the wrong lexeme; likely a mislinked entry.
findings.suggested: that, that thing (far from both speaker and listener)
findings.fix: that, that thing (far from both speaker and listener)

findings.issue: pt mirrors the かれ mix-up: 彼(あれ) does not mean 'ele'; it is the demonstrative 'aquilo/aquele'.
'boyfriend' is sense 2 of 彼(かれ), not of 彼(あれ). あれ's secondary personal use is 'that person (distant from both speaker and listener)'.
'namorado' renders the かれ 'boyfriend' gloss; wrong lexeme for 彼(あれ).

接見 ('audience; legal visit to a detainee') is an advanced formal/legal word, absent from N5 lists. The actual N5 word read せっけん is 石鹸 'soap' — this looks like a homophone mislink. Glosses are correct for 接見, but the item does not belong in an N5 course.
findings.suggested: relink entry to 石鹸(せっけん) 'soap' or drop from N5
findings.fix: relink entry to 石鹸(せっけん) 'soap' or drop from N5

findings.issue: 'aquilo' is a standalone neuter pronoun (= あれ) and can never modify a noun, while あの (adj-pn) is strictly prenominal. Listing it conflates あの with あれ — a core N5 distinction the course must keep clean.
戸(と) is a door / sliding panel (incl. shutters); a gate is 門. JMdict 1266970 lists no 'gate' sense, so 'gate' teaches a wrong equivalence.
'portão' = 門, aligned with the incorrect en gloss 'gate'. Also 'porta (de correr)' over-narrows — 戸 is any door, especially sliding.
'em ponto' means 'sharp / exactly on the hour' (Japanese ちょうど), a nuance the suffix 時 does not carry; 時 attaches even to non-exact times (3時15分). Learner may think 3時 means '3 em ponto'.
findings.suggested: hora (sufixo), horas (ao dizer as horas: 3時 = três horas)
findings.fix: hora (sufixo), horas (ao dizer as horas: 3時 = três horas)

findings.issue: "abafado" means muggy/stuffy (humid, poorly ventilated) — the standard pt-BR equivalent of 蒸し暑い, not plain 暑い. It is absent from the EN gloss "hot (weather, air)" and blurs the distinction with mushiatsui.
notes: "Abafado" = muggy/stuffy, the standard pt-BR match for 蒸し暑い. A dry-hot day is 暑い but never abafado; the gloss adds a humidity component absent from 暑い and the EN gloss. Dropping it is correct.

findings.issue: 杯 read さかずき means specifically a sake cup (small cup for alcoholic drinks), not a generic cup/glass. Leading glosses 'cup' and 'glass' belong to コップ/カップ or the counter 杯(はい); they teach the learner that さかずき is the everyday word for any cup or glass, which is false.
findings.suggested: sake cup, cup for alcoholic beverages
findings.fix: sake cup, cup for alcoholic beverages

findings.issue: Mirrors the EN defect: 'copo' and 'taça' are generic drinking-vessel words (コップ/カップ), wrong for さかずき, which is specifically the small cup used for saquê. Only 'cálice (de saquê)' is correct.
findings.suggested: cálice de saquê, taça para bebidas alcoólicas
findings.fix: cálice de saquê, taça para bebidas alcoólicas

findings.issue: This sense belongs to the homophone 付ける (to write down; to keep a diary/records), not 点ける. 点ける only means to turn on / light (fire, candle, cigarette); 日記を点ける is incorrect kanji usage, so the entry teaches a false meaning.
findings.current: to keep (a diary, records); to make an entry
findings.suggested: to light (a candle, cigarette); to set fire to
findings.fix: to light (a candle, cigarette); to set fire to

findings.issue: Mirrors the homophone error in the EN gloss: 'manter (um diário)' renders a sense of 付ける, not 点ける. The second sense of 点ける is lighting/igniting, not record-keeping.
'roupa para lavar' denotes the laundry items, which is 洗濯物, not 洗濯. 洗濯 refers only to the act of washing; this gloss teaches a wrong noun referent (learner may say 洗濯を畳む instead of 洗濯物を畳む).
'palito de acender' is not an idiomatic pt-BR collocation; Brazilians say 'palito de fósforo' or just 'fósforo'. The parenthetical disambiguator should use natural wording.
生る(なる) means 'to bear fruit' (of plants, JMdict 1611000). The glosses given belong to the homophone 成る/為る 'to become' (JMdict 1375610). The entry teaches a false meaning for this exact hw+kana pair.
findings.current: to become, to turn into, to come to be
findings.suggested: to bear fruit; to be produced (of fruit)
findings.fix: to bear fruit; to be produced (of fruit)

findings.issue: pt mirrors the homophone's meaning: 生る means 'dar fruto' (planta que produz fruto), not 'tornar-se/virar' (that is 成る). Sense-changing mistranslation.

'assunto' (topic/subject under discussion) is not a meaning of 物; that is 事/話題. The abstract sense of もの is 'things (in general/situation)', already covered by 'as coisas (situação)'. A learner would wrongly use 物 for 'assunto'.
findings.suggested: as coisas (situação), as coisas em geral
findings.fix: as coisas (situação), as coisas em geral

findings.issue: Gloss belongs to the homophone 達 (tachi, JMdict 1416220), the pluralizing suffix. This entry (1551240, 立ち) means departure/setting off, being used up, rehearsal, etc. — never a plural suffix. If the plural suffix was intended (it is the N5 word), the record should be re-keyed to 達.
Faithful translation of the wrong English gloss: 立ち is not the plural suffix (that is 達). Must be fixed together with senses[0].en; the plural-suffix meaning teaches a false kanji-word association.

"To pass (of time)" is the meaning of the homophone verb 経つ (たつ), a separate lexeme. JMdict 1597040 立つ has no time-elapse sense; writing 時間が立つ is nonstandard. Replace with a genuine 立つ sense (e.g. to depart/leave, JMdict senses 4-5) or delete the sense.
findings.suggested: to depart (on a trip); to leave
findings.fix: to depart (on a trip); to leave

findings.issue: Renders the 経つ meaning ("passar (tempo); decorrer"), which does not belong to 立つ. Must be fixed together with senses[2].en to whatever genuine 立つ sense replaces it.

EN sense is the belittling "the likes of" (JMdict: lessening the significance of the previous word), but the pt renders the neutral "things/something like" — duplicating sense 1 and losing the derogatory/humbling nuance that is the whole point of this sense.

Sense belongs to the homophone 掛かる, not 罹る. The headword 罹る only means 'to suffer from / to catch (an illness)' (already covered by senses[1]). Teaching 'to take (time)/to cost (money)' under 罹る is false; the pt 'levar (tempo), custar (dinheiro)' mirrors the same error.
findings.suggested: (remove this sense — glosses belong to 掛かる; 罹る means only 'to catch / suffer from an illness')
findings.fix: (remove this sense — glosses belong to 掛かる; 罹る means only 'to catch / suffer from an illness')

findings.issue: Gloss 'por aqui (área)' is a deictic adverbial phrase, not a noun: the 'here' meaning comes from この in この辺, not from 辺 itself. Glossing the bare noun as 'por aqui' misleads learners into thinking 辺 alone means 'around here' and mismatches the noun POS.

'To hold (an event)/to open (a show)' is a sense of the transitive reading 開く（ひらく）, not of intransitive あく (tagged vi). あく never takes an event object; this teaches a false usage (×パーティーをあく). Replace with a real あく sense, e.g. opening for business.
findings.current: to hold (an event); to open (a show)

findings.issue: pt mirrors the wrong-lexeme sense: 'realizar (um evento), promover' belongs to 開く（ひらく）(transitive), not to intransitive あく. Must be replaced together with the en gloss (e.g. shop opening for business).

Invented sense not in JMdict: the conjunction だから only means 'so/therefore' (it introduces a result). 'because/since (giving a reason)' is the gloss of から/ので — the causal direction is reversed, so this sense teaches another word's meaning.
findings.suggested: (remove sense 2 — covered by sense 1 'so; therefore'; 'because' belongs to から/ので)
findings.fix: (remove sense 2 — covered by sense 1 'so; therefore'; 'because' belongs to から/ので)

findings.issue: Mirrors the invented EN sense: 'porque/já que/pois' introduce a reason clause, which だから can never do (it introduces the consequence). A Brazilian learner would produce cause-effect-reversed sentences.
findings.suggested: (remover o sentido — だから corresponde a 'por isso/portanto', nunca introduz motivo como 'porque')
findings.fix: (remover o sentido — だから corresponde a 'por isso/portanto', nunca introduz motivo como 'porque')

findings.issue: JMdict sense 2 of すると is inferential ('then (in that case); if that is the case; if so' — drawing a conclusion from what was just said). 'if (one does), then' misdescribes it as the conditional 〜と pattern and largely duplicates sense 1, while the real must-know sense is lost.

Follows the garbled EN gloss: 'se... então'/'quando... então' present すると as a conditional 'if...then' connective; the actual sense is inferential, used to draw a conclusion ('nesse caso; sendo assim').

Sense 'to get thirsty; to be parched' belongs to the homophone lexeme 渇く (kawaku, thirst), not 乾く. JMdict keeps them as separate entries; 乾く means only 'to become dry'. The pt glosses 'ficar com sede, ressecar (garganta)' carry the same wrong-lexeme meaning.
findings.current: to get thirsty; to be parched
findings.suggested: (delete this sense — 'to get thirsty' is 渇く, a different lexeme; 乾く means only 'to dry / to become dry')
findings.fix: (delete this sense — 'to get thirsty' is 渇く, a different lexeme; 乾く means only 'to dry / to become dry')

findings.issue: 'konya' does not unambiguously render こんや: in wapuro input 'n'+'ya' resolves to にゃ (konya → こにゃ). Syllabic ん before や needs an apostrophe.

'To reflect (an image); to project' are glosses of the homophone 映す (utsusu), not 写す. 写す means to copy/photograph/depict. Also, 写す's must-know core sense 'to photograph' is missing from the entry; it should replace this sense.
findings.suggested: to photograph; to take a picture
findings.fix: to photograph; to take a picture

findings.issue: 'Refletir (uma imagem); projetar' translates the homophone 映す, not 写す. Should carry 写す's missing core photo sense instead.
'To pass on (a cold), to infect' is a gloss of the homophone 移す (utsusu, e.g. 風邪を移す), not 写す. A real remaining sense of 写す is 'to describe/depict'.
findings.current: to pass on (a cold), to infect

findings.issue: 'Transmitir (resfriado), contagiar' translates the homophone 移す, not 写す. Should match the corrected EN sense (describe/depict).
Core noun meaning 'departure' is missing. pos is [n, vs, vi] and every other suru-noun in this batch (入学, 入院, 冷房, 利用, 出席) includes the nominal gloss; 出発 gives only verbal glosses.
findings.current: to depart; to leave; to set off

findings.issue: Missing the nominal gloss 'partida' matching the n pos; also 'ir embora' (to go away for good) drifts from 出発 (to set off/depart on a journey) and is best dropped.
Romaji 'genin' does not match the kana げんいん: it reads as げにん (ge-ni-n). Syllabic ん before a vowel requires disambiguation, e.g. gen'in. This is a kana-mismatch, not a wapuro style variant.

'To visit' is the meaning of the homophone 訪ねる (also read たずねる), a separate lexeme. 尋ねる means to ask/inquire and, secondarily, to search/look for (JMdict sense 2). Teaching 尋ねる = visit confuses the classic N4 confusable pair 尋ねる vs 訪ねる.
'visitar, ir ver' renders the homophone 訪ねる, not 尋ねる. If the EN sense is corrected to the real second sense of 尋ねる (to search/look for), the pt must follow.
'preguiça (de levantar)' means laziness/reluctance to get up, not the act of oversleeping; a learner could wrongly equate 寝坊 with 'preguiça'. The first gloss 'dormir demais' is correct.

おる is the humble/courteous counterpart of いる (JMdict tags it [hum]), but both en and pt gloss it as plain neutral 'to be'. Using おる neutrally (e.g. about the listener or a teacher) sounds rude or dialectal. Sibling entries like 差し上げる do mark humility in the gloss; this one should too.
findings.current: to be (animate); to exist; to stay
findings.suggested: to be (animate; humble); to exist; to stay
findings.fix: to be (animate; humble); to exist; to stay

findings.issue: Syllabic ん before a vowel needs an apostrophe: 'tenin' transliterates てにん, not てんいん. This is a reading ambiguity, not a style choice.
彼ら refers to male or mixed groups (JMdict: 'usually of males'); an all-female group is 彼女たち/彼女ら. Glossing it as 'elas' invites learners to use 彼ら for a group of women.
ございます by itself is the polite existence verb (polite ある), not a copula — the copula is でございます. It is also polite (丁寧語), not humble. The parenthetical teaches wrong grammar terminology.
Garbled parenthetical: 'to strike (a clock the hour)' is not grammatical English; a word or separator is missing. Meaning (clock striking the hour) is correct but the wording needs a rewrite.
findings.suggested: to strike (the hour; of a clock)
findings.fix: to strike (the hour; of a clock)

findings.issue: pt gloss list includes 'programa', which is the meaning of 番組 (TV/radio program), not 放送 (the act of broadcasting / a transmission). It has no counterpart in the en glosses and blurs a distinction JLPT materials test; a learner could say 放送 when they mean 番組.
findings.current: transmissão, programa, transmitir, ir ao ar

findings.issue: 楽しみ sense 2 is a noun/adj-na sense ('anticipation; something to look forward to'), but the pt gloss 'ansiar por' is a verb phrase ('to long for'). Word-class mismatch with the lemma's pos (no verb pos on this entry); the meaning is adjacent but the category is wrong.

The gloss 'largo da costa' is malformed Portuguese as a standalone noun gloss; the idiom is 'ao largo da costa' (off the coast). Without 'ao', 'largo' reads as the adjective 'wide', which can confuse learners.

"picada" in Brazilian Portuguese primarily means an insect bite or the needle prick itself, not the injection; the parenthetical "(vacina)" also wrongly narrows 注射 to vaccines. Natural BR rendering of "shot" is "injeção" or "dose (de vacina)".
"descer ladeira esquiando" is awkward, non-idiomatic Brazilian Portuguese (missing article; "ladeira" is a sloped street, not a ski slope — ski context uses "pista"/"encosta").

Gloss 'to be vacant' belongs to the homophone reading 空く(あく). 空く(すく) means to become less crowded/empty (電車がすく); it is not used for a vacant seat/room, which is あく. This imports the other lexeme's gloss and invites the classic あく/すく misuse.
findings.current: to be empty | to be uncrowded | to be vacant
findings.suggested: to be empty | to be uncrowded
findings.fix: to be empty | to be uncrowded

findings.issue: Romaji 'honyaku' is ambiguous: syllabic n before ya requires an apostrophe, otherwise it reads as ho-nya-ku (ほにゃく), not ほんやく. Needs 'hon'yaku'.
'cumprimentar' primarily means 'to greet' in pt-BR; listed bare it suggests homeru = greet someone. For 'to compliment/commend' the natural pt-BR is 'parabenizar' or 'fazer um elogio'.

見える 'to come' is sonkeigo (honorific: the subject is a respected other), not merely polite. '(polite)'/'(cortês)' invites learners to use it for their own coming. The batch's own convention marks keigo category precisely (致す = 'to do (humble)').
'erva' alone reads as 'herb' (colloquially also marijuana slang); the standard pt-BR term for the 'weed' sense is 'erva daninha'.
Sense 'counter for houses' belongs to a different lexeme: 軒 read けん (ken). For this hw+kana pair (軒/のき) the word means only 'eaves'. The pt 'contador de casas' repeats the same error.
findings.suggested: Remove this sense entirely (counter usage is 軒・けん, not のき)
findings.fix: Remove this sense entirely (counter usage is 軒・けん, not のき)

findings.issue: 'brinde' in pt-BR primarily means a promotional freebie/giveaway (or a toast), not a personal gift; misleading as a gloss for 贈り物 'gift, present'.

Sense 2 glosses 'to be known as / to pass as' belong to 通る (とおる), not 通う (e.g. 天才で通っている). 通う's actual secondary senses are 'to be conveyed (of feelings)' / 'to circulate (of blood)'. The pt list ('ser conhecido como', 'passar por') mirrors the same wrong sense.
findings.current: to be known as, to pass as
findings.suggested: remove sense (belongs to 通る); or replace with: to be conveyed (of feelings)
findings.fix: remove sense (belongs to 通る); or replace with: to be conveyed (of feelings)

findings.issue: 'correr' alone means 'to run' (= 走る), not 'to run away'; listing it as a gloss of 逃げる invites the learner to confuse the two verbs. The EN list correctly has no plain 'to run'.
'atrapalho' is not a standard noun in Brazilian Portuguese (the derived noun is 'atrapalhação'); it reads as an improvised form in a dictionary gloss.

Gloss 'sem jeito' in pt-BR primarily means 'awkward/embarrassed' (ficar sem jeito) or 'clumsy', not 'no good/useless/hopeless'. The intended idiom is 'não tem jeito'; as a bare gloss it suggests a wrong meaning for だめ.

Gloss "tu" is register-neutral (and regional/pt-PT-flavored for most Brazilians), losing the rough/condescending nuance that defines お前; unmarked it can mislead a learner into treating お前 as ordinary informal 'you'.
In the 'far (away) / way (off)' sense, bare "muito" does not render distance (it duplicates sense 2's intensifier meaning), and "bem mais longe" adds a comparative 'mais' not present in the sense.

'sorridentemente' is a virtually unused -mente coinage in Brazilian Portuguese; it reads as a machine-translation of 'smilingly'. The other two glosses are natural; this one would be replaced by any BR reviewer.

Romaji 'bonyari' is ambiguous for ぼんやり: without a separator it reads as bo-nya-ri (ぼにゃり). Syllabic ん before や requires an apostrophe (Hepburn bon'yari) or doubled n in wapuro; as written it does not round-trip to the kana.

プロ is register-neutral in Japanese (e.g. プロ野球, formal news usage), but 'profissa' is informal Brazilian slang. Sense has register: null and no misc tag, so a slang gloss misrepresents the word's tone; 'profissional' alone covers the meaning.

Gloss 'the more ... (the more ...)' describes the correlative 〜ば〜ほど construction, not 一方(だ), which marks a trend that just keeps going in one direction (悪化する一方だ = 'just keeps getting worse'). Misleading for a core N3 grammar use; could teach learners to use 一方 in 'the more X, the more Y' sentences.

findings.issue: In Brazilian Portuguese 'ordinário' is read by default as pejorative (shoddy, vulgar, despicable person); as a bare gloss for 一般 'general/common' it invites embarrassing misuse (e.g. 'uma família ordinária'). Register trap for pt-BR learners.
